# njlea-api

This is the source code for the NJ Law Enforcement Agencies API deployed at
`api.tor-gu.com/nj/lea/`.

It serves [njlea](https://github.com/tor-gu/njlea), a registry of New Jersey law
enforcement agencies from 2020 to 2026. Each agency has a stable ID, its names over
time, its level of government and function, the municipalities it polices, its FBI
ORIs, and every spelling of it used by the NJ Office of the Attorney General (OAG)
datasets. Field names and values are the same as in the R package; see it for more
details on the underlying dataset.

## Try it out

### OpenAPI/Swagger
There is an OpenAPI/swagger document deployed [here](https://tor-gu.com/apis/njlea.html)
that you can play with. The spec is `njlea-openapi.yaml`.

### Endpoints

| Endpoint | R equivalent | Filters |
|---|---|---|
| `/nj/lea/agencies`, `/nj/lea/agencies/{year}` | `get_agencies(year)` | `county`, `agency_level`, `agency_function` |
| `/nj/lea/agencies/{year}/{agency_id}` | one row of `get_agencies(year)` | |
| `/nj/lea/agency_epochs` | the `agency` table | `agency_id` |
| `/nj/lea/agency_municipalities`, `/nj/lea/agency_municipalities/{year}` | `get_agency_municipalities(year, geoid_year)` | `geoid_year`, `agency_id`, `GEOID` |
| `/nj/lea/aliases` | the `agency_alias` table | `source`, `agency_id` |
| `/nj/lea/oris`, `/nj/lea/oris/{ori}` | the `agency_ori` table | `agency_id` |
| `/nj/lea/sources` | the `alias_source` table | |
| `/nj/lea/search?q=` | `find_agency(pattern, county, year)` | `county`, `year` |

Without a `{year}`, the latest year (2026) is used, and the reply's links give it
explicitly. `county` may be given as `Camden` or `Camden County`.

### Sample code
Each endpoint returns paginated results, with a `"next"` url in the `"links"` section
indicating that there are more results to be retrieved.

This is illustrated in the python code below, which loads the agencies of 2026 into a
[pandas DataFrame](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.html)
and counts them by level.
```{python}
import json
import requests
import pandas as pd

API_ROOT = r.API_ROOT


def load_as_df(url):
    """Retrieve entire dataset at url and return as a dataframe"""
    # Get the first page
    resp = requests.get(url)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    resp_json = json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8'))
    df = pd.DataFrame(resp_json["data"])

    # Keep retrieving pages while there is a 'next' link
    while "next" in resp_json["links"]:
        resp = requests.get(resp_json["links"]["next"])
        resp.raise_for_status()
        resp_json = json.loads(resp.content.decode('utf-8'))
        df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(resp_json["data"])], ignore_index=True)
    return df


agencies_2026 = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/agencies/2026")
by_level = agencies_2026.groupby("agency_level").size().reset_index(name="n")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
library(reticulate)
knitr::kable(head(py$agencies_2026))
knitr::kable(py$by_level)
```

#### Agencies serving several municipalities
`multi_municipal` is `true` for an agency linked to more than one municipality in the
year. It is `false` for agencies with no links at all, too: sheriffs, prosecutors,
state agencies and the NJ State Police.
```{python}
multi = agencies_2026[agencies_2026["multi_municipal"]]
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$multi)
```

#### Municipalities served
A municipal department's own municipality is its `Home` link; a municipality it
polices by agreement is a `Service` link. Camden County Police Department polices
Camden city, and took over Woodlynne in 2024 when the Woodlynne Police Department
disbanded:
```{python}
camden = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/agency_municipalities/2025?agency_id=NJLEA0132")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$camden)
```

`GEOID` is a US Census GEOID as of `geoid_year` (by default, the year), so it joins
to [njmunicipalities-api](https://tor-gu.com/apis/njmunicipalities.html). Here
are the municipalities of 2026 with no agency link. **NJ State Police links are not
included yet**: NJSP is the local police of many rural municipalities, but no
published list names them, so most of these are NJSP-patrolled, though not all.
```{python}
links_2026 = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/agency_municipalities/2026")
municipalities_2026 = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/municipalities/2026")
unlinked = municipalities_2026[~municipalities_2026["GEOID"].isin(links_2026["GEOID"])]
unlinked_by_county = unlinked.groupby("county").size().reset_index(name="n")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$unlinked_by_county)
```

#### Finding an agency
`/nj/lea/search` searches canonical names and every source spelling. `q` is a
case-insensitive substring, not a regular expression (unlike `find_agency()` in the R
package). Here a former name finds the Youth Justice Commission, which was the Juvenile
Justice Commission until March 2025:
```{python}
hits = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/search?q=juvenile%20justice")
epochs = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/agency_epochs?agency_id=NJLEA0539")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$hits)
knitr::kable(py$epochs[, c("agency_id", "first_year", "final_year", "agency_name")])
```

#### Joining to FBI data
ORIs are attributes, not keys: an agency can have several (the NJ State Police has 22)
or none. Join them to FBI Crime Data Explorer data on `ori`:
```{python}
rutgers = load_as_df(f"{API_ROOT}/nj/lea/oris?agency_id=NJLEA0543")
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(py$rutgers)
```

## Deploying
This API is implemented as an [AWS SAM](https://aws.amazon.com/serverless/sam/)
application: one Lambda function serves every route, with the data packaged in it. A
deployment has three parts:

1. The lambda layer [layer_torguapi](https://github.com/tor-gu/layer_torguapi) (version
   11 or later), which needs to be deployed separately.
2. The data: CSV exports of a tagged [njlea](https://github.com/tor-gu/njlea) release,
   committed in `data/`, and built into `lea/data/njlea.json` by `make data`.
3. The Lambda and API Gateway, defined in `template.yaml`.

### Data
`data/` holds the njlea tables, the njmunicipalities rows they reference, and `SOURCE`,
which records the releases they were exported from. The export also writes R's own
`get_agencies()` and `get_agency_municipalities()` for every year and `geoid_year` to
`tests/parity/expected/`, which the parity test requires the API to reproduce. To export a
release (this needs R and the `remotes` package; the release is installed into a
temporary library) and build the Lambda's data:
```
make export_data REF=v0.1.0
make data
```
`lea/data/njlea.json` is not committed; CI builds it with `make data` before testing and
before `sam build`.

### Data update
1. `make export_data REF=<new release>`, and review the diff in `data/`.
2. `make data parity_test example_test`. The year range and the default year come from
   the export, but the spec's examples, its year ranges and this README (then `make knit`)
   may need updating; the example test shows the new values.
3. Push to `dev`, check the dev API, then merge to `main`.

### Development
```
make venv          # .venv with the test, style and spec tools
make style unit_test
make data example_test parity_test
make apigateway_spec   # the spec for API Gateway, without examples
```
The unit tests import the torguapi layer from `./torguapi`; `scripts/fetch_torguapi.sh`
downloads it.

### Direct deploy
The application can be deployed directly using the SAM CLI:
```
make data apigateway_spec
sam build
sam deploy --stack-name MyStackName                                                         \
           --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM                                                    \
           --resolve-s3                                                                     \
           --parameter-overrides                                                            \
                TorguapiLayerArn=arn:aws:lambda:us-east-1:123456789012:layer:layer_torguapi \
                TorguapiLayerVersion=10                                                     \
                ApiRoot=https://api.example.com                                             \
                DataVersion=$(sed -n 's/^version=//p' data/SOURCE)
```
Replace the `TorguapiLayerXXX` params with the values derived from the `layer_torguapi`
deployment.

The `ApiRoot` value is used only for generating the values in `"links"` in the JSON reply.
On `api.tor-gu.com`, the relationship between the publicly facing API URL and the API
Gateway endpoints is configured in
[torgu-api-cloudfront](https://github.com/tor-gu/torgu-api-cloudfront).

To deploy a second environment alongside the first, give it a resource name prefix (I use
`dev-`) with the `EnvPrefix` template parameter.

### Using GitHub Actions
`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys from GitHub: a push to `dev` deploys the dev
stack and runs the integration tests against it, and a merge to `main` deploys prod. It
assumes AWS roles through GitHub's OIDC provider; the roles are defined in
`infra/github/` (Terraform).
